Only a contracting officer acting within their authority executes a modification; no one else may direct work belonging on one (RFO FAR 43.202(a), 1.402-1). My warrant must cover the cumulative contract value including the modification.

Types (43.203):
- Bilateral supplemental agreements, signed by both parties: equitable adjustments, letter contract definitization, other agreed changes; the only way to change a commercial contract (52.212-4(d)).
- Unilateral, signed only by me: administrative changes (43.201), change orders under the Changes clauses (43.301, 43.305), changes under other clauses such as Options, and termination notices.
- Only in-scope changes, including priced options evaluated in the competition, are exempt from Part 6 (6.001(c)); out-of-scope work needs competition or a J&A (6.103, 6.104).

Steps:
- Written requirement and scope determination; work someone already directed is a possible constructive change or unauthorized commitment (43.204, 1.405).
- Certified funds before adding money (43.205) and a SAM exclusions check (9.405-1(a)(2)).
- Price before execution if possible, or at least a ceiling (43.202(b)); certified data if the adjustment, counting increases and decreases, exceeds the contract threshold (15.403-3(b)(3)).
- Definitize change orders quickly, with a release (43.304); DoD unpriced change orders over $5 million need an NTE, a 180-day definitization schedule and a 50 percent obligation cap, or 75 percent after a qualifying proposal (DFARS 243.370).
- Sign the SF 30 (43.401) and report it in FPDS within three business days (4.301).

The VCE file (AFARS 5104.101(a)) must let a stranger rebuild the action (4.101): requirement, scope and funding records, exclusions check, option determinations (17.204-1(b)), analysis, objectives and PNM (15.408-1, 15.408-2), and signed SF 30s.

Cite: RFO FAR 1.402-1, 1.405, 4.101, 4.301, 6.001(c), 6.103, 6.104, 9.405-1(a)(2), 15.403-3(b)(3), 15.408-1, 15.408-2, 17.204-1(b), 43.201 through 43.205, 43.301, 43.304, 43.305, 43.401, 52.212-4(d); DFARS 243.370 (Class Deviation 2026-O0034 Rev. 1); AFARS 5104.101(a); Army Warranting Program Policy v12.
key_points: Only a KO acting within the scope of their authority (warrant) executes modifications, and no one else directs changed work (RFO FAR 43.202, 1.402-1); the warrant must cover the cumulative contract value including the modification (Army Warranting Program Policy v12); normally on SF 30 (43.401).

Bilateral supplemental agreement: equitable adjustments after change orders, letter-contract definitization, other agreed changes; commercial contracts change only by written agreement (RFO FAR 52.212-4(d)).
Unilateral: administrative changes, change orders under 52.243-1 to -5 within scope, changes under other clauses (Options, Property, Suspension of Work), termination notices (RFO FAR 43.203(b)).
Only in-scope modifications are exempt from Part 6 (RFO FAR 6.001(c)); out of scope = compete or J&A (6.103, 6.104).

Steps and file: written requirement and scope determination, certified funds (43.205), SAM exclusions check (9.405-1(a)(2)), proposal and analysis, certified data or exception (15.403-3(b)(3)), objectives and PNM (15.408-1, 15.408-2), signed SF 30, FPDS contract action report within three business days (4.301), all in VCE.

Unpriced change orders: ceiling price, definitize in the shortest practicable time on a second SF 30 with a release (43.202(b), 43.304); DoD over $5M: NTE, generally 180-day schedule, 50/75 percent obligation limits (RFO DFARS 243.370).

answer:
Because the file is the Government's memory and its evidence. Long after I have rotated out, it is the only thing that shows what was done and why.

RFO FAR 4.101 requires each contracting, administration and paying office to keep a file that comprehensively records the transaction history: a complete background for informed decisions at each step, clear support for every action taken, information for reviews and investigations, and the essential facts if litigation or a congressional inquiry arises. 44 U.S.C. 3101 puts the same records duty on every agency.

A complete file:
- Proves the action was proper - authority, compliance, funds and fair treatment, which is what RFO FAR 1.402-1 and 1.402-2 hold me to. If it is not in the file, a reviewer will treat it as not done.
- Defends the decision. In a protest, GAO gives little weight to new analyses prepared in the heat of the protest and credits later explanations only when they fit the record made at the time; in a claim, the Government's case is built from the file.
- Survives turnover. Files are kept six years after final payment (RFO FAR 4.309), and a claim can be submitted up to six years after it accrues (41 U.S.C. 7103(a)(4)(A)).
- Feeds everything downstream: the FPDS contract action report (4.301), closeout under 4.308, audits and reviews.

In the Army the file lives in VCE (AFARS 5104.101(a)), and I build it as the action happens, not at closeout.

Cite: RFO FAR 4.101, 1.402-1, 1.402-2, 4.301, 4.308, 4.309; AFARS 5104.101(a); 44 U.S.C. 3101; 41 U.S.C. 7103(a)(4)(A).
key_points: RFO FAR 4.101 (old subpart 4.8): every contracting, administration and paying office keeps a file that comprehensively records the transaction history.
Four purposes: informed decisions, clear support for actions, reviews and investigations, litigation and congressional inquiries; 44 U.S.C. 3101 puts the records duty on every agency.
Proves the action was proper - authority, compliance, funds, fair treatment (RFO FAR 1.402-1, 1.402-2); if it is not in the file, it was not done.

Defends protests and claims: GAO gives little weight to post-protest reevaluations and credits later explanations only when consistent with the contemporaneous record (Boeing Sikorsky Aircraft Support, B-277263.2, 1997).
Continuity: files kept 6 years after final payment (RFO FAR 4.309); claims can be submitted up to 6 years after accrual (41 U.S.C. 7103(a)(4)(A)).
Feeds the FPDS contract action report (4.301), closeout (4.308), audits and reviews; Army files live in VCE (AFARS 5104.101(a)) and are built as the action happens.
